```json
{
  "schema": "redline.threatmodel.v1",
  "issueKey": "EVAL-02",
  "sketch": {
    "components": ["Product page UI", "Comment form", "Rich text editor", "Comments database", "Comment renderer", "Admin panel"],
    "dataStores": ["comments database"],
    "externalServices": [],
    "trustBoundaries": ["User browser to backend", "Database to rendering", "Regular users to moderators"],
    "dataClasses": [],
    "exposure": "public",
    "llmFeatures": false
  },
  "threats": [
    {
      "stride": "InformationDisclosure",
      "title": "Stored XSS in rich-text comments steals user sessions",
      "scenario": "An attacker posts a comment containing JavaScript in the rich text. When any visitor views the product page, the script executes in their browser, stealing their session cookie and sending it to the attacker. The attacker can then impersonate that user.",
      "component": "Comment renderer",
      "likelihood": 5,
      "impact": 5,
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "post comments with rich text (bold, links, images)" },
        { "quote": "rendered for every visitor" }
      ],
      "asvs": ["V5.3.3", "V5.3.6"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-79"],
      "plainLanguage": "An attacker can inject JavaScript into comments that runs when anyone views the page, stealing their login session",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Sanitize rich-text comment HTML",
        "given": "a user submits a comment with rich text formatting",
        "when": "the system stores and displays the comment",
        "then": "all HTML is sanitized to allow only safe tags (b, i, a with restricted href, img with restricted src) and all JavaScript is removed"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "ElevationOfPrivilege",
      "title": "XSS in comments hijacks moderator accounts",
      "scenario": "An attacker posts a comment with embedded JavaScript. When a moderator views the admin screen to review comments, the script executes with the moderator's privileges, performing actions like deleting other comments or creating new malicious ones.",
      "component": "Admin panel",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 5,
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "Moderators can delete comments from an admin screen" },
        { "quote": "post comments with rich text (bold, links, images)" }
      ],
      "asvs": ["V5.3.3", "V14.4.1"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-79"],
      "plainLanguage": "Malicious JavaScript in a comment can take over a moderator's account when they view the moderation panel",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Render comments safely in admin panel",
        "given": "a moderator views the admin panel showing user comments",
        "when": "comments contain rich text or HTML",
        "then": "the content is displayed with the same sanitization as the public site, preventing script execution"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "Tampering",
      "title": "HTML injection breaks page layout and misleads users",
      "scenario": "An attacker submits a comment with unclosed HTML tags or oversized elements. When other users view the product page, the page layout breaks, text becomes unreadable, or legitimate content is hidden, making users distrust the site or miss important information.",
      "component": "Comment renderer",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 3,
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "post comments with rich text (bold, links, images)" },
        { "quote": "rendered for every visitor" }
      ],
      "asvs": ["V5.3.3"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-79"],
      "plainLanguage": "An attacker can submit malformed HTML that breaks the page layout or covers up legitimate content",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Validate and close HTML tags in comments",
        "given": "a user submits rich-text with HTML",
        "when": "the system renders the comment",
        "then": "all tags are closed properly, oversized elements are constrained, and the HTML cannot break out of the comment container"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "Spoofing",
      "title": "Phishing links disguised in comment text",
      "scenario": "An attacker posts a comment with a link that appears to go to a legitimate site (e.g., display text 'Click here for support') but actually redirects to a phishing site. Users click the link, enter credentials on the fake site, and the attacker steals their accounts.",
      "component": "Comment form",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 4,
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "rich text (bold, links, images)" }
      ],
      "asvs": ["V5.1.1"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-601"],
      "plainLanguage": "Attackers can post links that look safe but lead to phishing or malware sites",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Validate and mark external links",
        "given": "a comment contains a hyperlink",
        "when": "the link is rendered",
        "then": "external links open in a new tab with rel='noopener noreferrer', are clearly marked as external, and links to untrusted domains may be blocked or require user confirmation"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "Tampering",
      "title": "CSRF allows posting comments as another user",
      "scenario": "An attacker creates a malicious website that submits a comment form request to this product page. When a logged-in user visits the attacker's site, their browser unknowingly posts a comment under their account, spreading spam or inappropriate content attributed to them.",
      "component": "Comment form",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "Logged-in customers can post comments" }
      ],
      "asvs": ["V4.2.2"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-352"],
      "plainLanguage": "An attacker's website can trick a user's browser into posting comments without their knowledge",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Protect comment submission with CSRF token",
        "given": "a user submits a comment",
        "when": "the backend processes the request",
        "then": "a valid, unguessable CSRF token specific to that user's session must be present, and requests without it are rejected"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "InformationDisclosure",
      "title": "External image URLs track comment viewers",
      "scenario": "An attacker posts a comment with an image hosted on their own server. When users view the product page, their browsers load the image, sending the user's IP address, browser fingerprint, and timestamp to the attacker's server, tracking who views the page.",
      "component": "Comment renderer",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 2,
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "rich text (bold, links, images)" },
        { "quote": "rendered for every visitor" }
      ],
      "asvs": ["V5.1.3"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-918"],
      "plainLanguage": "Images in comments can be used to track who views the page by loading them from an attacker's server",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Proxy or restrict external images",
        "given": "a comment contains an image URL",
        "when": "the image is displayed to users",
        "then": "images are either hosted on the application's domain after upload and validation, or proxied through the application to hide user IP addresses"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "DenialOfService",
      "title": "Comment spam overwhelms product pages",
      "scenario": "An attacker uses automated tools to rapidly post hundreds or thousands of comments on popular product pages. Legitimate comments become buried, page load times increase significantly, and the database storage and rendering resources are exhausted.",
      "component": "Comment form",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 3,
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "Logged-in customers can post comments" }
      ],
      "asvs": [],
      "cwe": ["CWE-770"],
      "plainLanguage": "An attacker can flood product pages with spam comments, burying legitimate content and slowing down the site",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Rate-limit comment posting per user",
        "given": "a logged-in user attempts to post multiple comments",
        "when": "they exceed a reasonable threshold (e.g., 5 per minute, 20 per hour)",
        "then": "further comment submissions are blocked temporarily and the user sees a rate limit message"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "Repudiation",
      "title": "No audit trail for comment authorship and changes",
      "scenario": "An attacker posts illegal or defamatory content in a comment, then deletes or edits it. When moderators investigate or legal action is pursued, there is no record of who posted the original content, when it was posted, or what was changed.",
      "component": "Comments database",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "Logged-in customers can post comments" },
        { "quote": "Comments are stored in the comments database" }
      ],
      "asvs": ["V7.1.1", "V7.1.2"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-778"],
      "plainLanguage": "The system may not keep a record of who posted or modified comments, making it impossible to investigate abuse",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Log all comment actions with user and timestamp",
        "given": "a user creates, edits, or deletes a comment",
        "when": "the action is performed",
        "then": "the system logs the user ID, timestamp, action type, and content (or content hash) in an append-only audit log"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "ElevationOfPrivilege",
      "title": "Comment deletion accessible to non-moderators",
      "scenario": "The admin screen for deleting comments checks only that the user is logged in, not that they have moderator privileges. Any logged-in customer can access the delete function, allowing them to remove competitors' positive comments or legitimate criticism.",
      "component": "Admin panel",
      "likelihood": 2,
      "impact": 4,
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "Moderators can delete comments from an admin screen" }
      ],
      "asvs": ["V4.1.1", "V4.2.1"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-862"],
      "plainLanguage": "The comment deletion feature might not properly check if the user is actually a moderator",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Restrict comment deletion to moderators only",
        "given": "a user attempts to access the comment deletion function",
        "when": "the backend processes the request",
        "then": "the system verifies the user has the moderator role, and rejects the request with 403 Forbidden if they do not"
      }
    }
  ]
}
```
